subject.title: fix(infra): bound gateway TLS file reads via secret-file helper

question: Should gateway TLS permanently reject certificate or key files above 64 KiB and CA bundles above 256 KiB during startup?
rationale: The implementation is sound, but selecting these previously undocumented limits intentionally changes which existing gateway TLS configurations are accepted and can make an upgraded gateway fail to start.

options.title: Approve the proposed limits
options.body: Accept 64 KiB for certificate/key files and 256 KiB for CA bundles as the supported gateway TLS contract, then land the proven patch.

options.title: Choose broader limits first
options.body: Raise or consolidate the bounds and update the focused tests before merge if maintainers need a wider compatibility window.

options.title: Pause fixed-limit hardening
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until representative production certificate-chain and CA-bundle sizes establish an acceptable contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed limits
recommendation.body: Accept 64 KiB for certificate/key files and 256 KiB for CA bundles as the supported gateway TLS contract, then land the proven patch.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged gateway TLS work provides the strongest available history signal for deciding listener-startup and upgrade behavior.
